 Most recent Most popular 'It's about who gets the next goal' published at 18:00 GMT 18:00 GMT 
 Nottm Forest 2-0 Man City 
 Steve Stone 
Former England midfielder on BBC Radio 5 live 
 It's about how Man City react from that and who gets the next goal.
 It makes Forest's life easier but it also makes them nervous when it's only 25 minutes played.
 14 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'This goal shows everyone Rodrigo is here' published at 17:59 GMT 17:59 GMT 
 FT: Fulham 1-1 Newcastle 
 Fulham 
 Fulham striker Rodrigo Muniz, speaking to Premier League Studios: "Last game was really difficult against Aston Villa then this week we trained hard, we knew this would be a tough game.
 "Newcastle have some really good players so happy to score to help my team-mates.
 "I train hard every week to get a chance to play and to score. I need to be ready. In the first half, I said to Kevin 'I need to be ready, I need to warm-up good and when I come on I need to do everything'.
 "Last season was really difficult for me. This goal was really important for me. Last season, I scored only one goal, not good. I want to play more and this goal shows everyone Rodrigo is here."
 27 11 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 17:58 GMT 17:58 GMT 
 Nottm Forest 2-0 Man City 
 City fans, what is going wrong here?
 Has Enzo Maresca got his team set up wrong? Where are the errors coming from?
 189 49 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'City are feeling massive pressure' published at 17:56 GMT 17:56 GMT 
 Nottm Forest 2-0 Man City 
 Steve Stone 
Former England midfielder on BBC Radio 5 live 
 These are superstar footballers but if you put a bit of pressure on them, with a bit of work rate, all of a sudden they're feeling a massive pressure. 
 There's always a Forest player in a Man City players face. 
 418 56 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 17:56 GMT 17:56 GMT 
 Nottm Forest 2-0 Man City 
 Manchester City should probably have a goal back.
 Marc Guehi sends a lovely ball into the box and Enzo Fernandez has a free header but he sends it over the bar.
 134 81 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 17:55 GMT 17:55 GMT 
 Use 'Get involved' to have your say 
 If Man City don’t win today I can’t see them catching up to Arsenal unless something miraculous happens and Arsenal crumble but I can’t see that happening. 6 points behind the current Premier League champions is a big gap even if it’s early in the season.
 Sakinah, Birmingham 
 439 427 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 17:55 GMT 17:55 GMT 
 Nottm Forest 2-0 Man City 
 Manchester City give away a fairly cheap corner but Abdukodir Khusanov was taking no chances with another promising Forest attack.
 City don't quite clear the ball and it comes to Murillo but his effort is tame and straight at Gianluigi Donnarumma.
 78 27 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'A very, very big experience' published at 17:54 GMT 17:54 GMT 
 FT: Arsenal 1-0 Hull 
 Hull City 
 Hull boss Sergej Jakirovic speaking to BBC MOTD: "We need to take lessons. I think this team is still growing. It is a very, very big experience for us to compete at this level and especially against Arsenal.
 "We have to continue like this and to fight. We tried to press them and push them forward. They were trying to play short passes. It isn't easy because you spend a lot of energy and every player for them can pass you.
 "I am very pleased. We have to continue, every game for us is a big lesson.
 "It was bad fortune [for the goal]. Maybe we could stop the second ball for their goal.
 "Sometimes I feel sorry because we had three home games and we had the lead and maybe could be more clever in these situations but it is all experience. 
 "We have to do everything in the next games to reach at least one win."
 76 19 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 17:53 GMT 17:53 GMT 
 Nottm Forest 2-0 Man City 
 This is the earliest Man City have been 2-0 down in a Premier League match (18th min) since November 2019 (13th minute at Liverpool).

 'City are all over the place' published at 17:53 GMT 17:53 GMT 
 Nottm Forest 2-0 Man City 
 Steve Stone 
Former Nottingham Forest midfielder on BBC Radio 5 live 
 Man City in the middle of the park they lose the ball. Liam Delap is one-on-one with about 40 yards to run in. 
 He drives and drives, into the box and then his right foot. He smashes it, there's no finesse in what he's trying to do there. It's past Gianluigi Donnarumma before he gets his hand up to it. 
 City are all over the place. 
 531 56 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 17:52 GMT 17:52 GMT 
 Nottm Forest 2-0 Man City 
 Manchester City are absolutely all over the place here.
 Another error sees the ball at the feet of Forest and Morgan Gibbs-White slides across for James McAtee who tries to sweep home but it's way over the bar.
 336 50 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 City wheels wobbling badly published at 17:51 GMT 17:51 GMT 
 Nottm Forest 2-0 Man City 
 Shamoon Hafez 
Football reporter at the City Ground 
 City are all over the place at the back and Forest are taking full advantage.
 This is turning into an incredible story.
 The home fans can't believe what they are seeing.
 604 90 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 GOAL - Nottm Forest 2-0 Man City published at 17:49 GMT 17:49 GMT 
 Liam Delap (18 mins) 
 WOW.
 Well Liam Delap has had his struggles in front of goal but a it's another big error from the visitors that sees him cash in.
 The ball is lost in the middle of the park and Xaver Schlager picks it up, laying it off for Delap who gets on a charging run.
 No tackle comes in and he powers towards goal before finishing who into the back of the net.
 Image source, Getty Images 
 2604 340 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'It is time to praise my players' published at 17:49 GMT 17:49 GMT 
 FT: Arsenal 1-0 Hull 
 Arsenal 
 Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, speaking to BBC MOTD: "Very happy with the performance and the victory as well. I think it is time to praise my players. What they have done not only today but after the international break is remarkable because of the games.
 "We had to wait and be patient in the last part of the game to make the difference and win the game. We kept generating chances, the final pass was missing or the last shot was blocked. We said at half-time if this is the case it will go all the way to full time but at some point it would come.
 "We have some great moments, we need to put the chances we are creating against the opponent into the scoreline, That is what we need to improve."
 On the decision not to award Arsenal a penalty: "I don't know. When they called the referee to the monitor I thought it was a penalty but then I heard the decision was made because of the offside decision. We don't have clarity on it."
 174 114 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 17:48 GMT 17:48 GMT 
 Nottm Forest 1-0 Man City 
 Former Manchester City man James McAtee swings the ball in and Gianluigi Donnarumma does not look comfortable as he leaps for the ball.
 Luckily for him it goes out for a goal kick.
 95 47 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 17:47 GMT 17:47 GMT 
 Nottm Forest 1-0 Man City 
 Iliman Ndiaye slips the ball through for Rayan Cherki and it's clipped across for Jeremy Doku but eventually goes out for a City throw-in.
 Cherki gives it away and a decent ball releases Liam Delap, who hesitates on the ball but eventually Forest win a corner.
 87 25 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We can compete at this level' published at 17:45 GMT 17:45 GMT 
 FT: Arsenal 1-0 Hull 
 Hull City 
 Hull manager Sergej Jakirovic to Sky Sports: "Unfortunately we conceded a cheap goal. But when you have [Noni] Madueke in the box 10 times, Elliot Stroud played a very good game today, it's not easy to stop him. After we save the ball maybe we can clear but what can we do?
 "We were brave, especially in the defensive phase, we didn't allow a lot of space. But also on the ball maybe we need much better decisions to be more brave in quick transitions. If we have this then we can be dangerous. But congratulations to both teams, I think the crowd had fun today.
 "It's very difficult, we had two players with cramp and also we tried to close the midfield zone today because Arsenal are doing everything to overload the midfield and it is not easy to control.
 "We have shown we can compete at this level. We have chances. This team is still growing because we bought a lot of new players. We can use this to take lessons for future games."
 120 19 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Defensive issues for City published at 17:44 GMT 17:44 GMT 
 Nottm Forest 1-0 Man City 
 Shamoon Hafez 
Football reporter at the City Ground 
 One clean sheet in the past 10 games for Manchester City now, on a day when champions Arsenal managed another shut out.
 Can't keep conceding goals and expecting to challenge for the title.
 324 71 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 17:44 GMT 17:44 GMT 
 Nottm Forest 1-0 Man City 
 Marc Guehi lets Morgan Gibbs-White get away from him and, although he recovers, the ball stays with Forest and comes to James McAtee on the right but his shot is straight at Gianluigi Donnarumma.
 Forest just carving through this City defence at the moment.
 173 27 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Madueke is an example to rest of the group' published at 17:43 GMT 17:43 GMT 
 FT: Arsenal 1-0 Hull 
 Arsenal 
 Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta to Sky Sports on how his side found their win: "Consistency and keep going. We talked about this that it will happen at some point to break them down. We had some big moments that in my opinion we should have scored some goals but we don't hit the target, we don't get the final pass. So many situations where if you don't do that you have to rely on generating so much volume and at some point relying that you will get them down and that's the way we won the game.
 "It's something that is happening a lot, and a few games as well we have been 1-0 down very early and we still manage to do that. Getting results is very, very important and I think we need to praise our players for the way they go about every single game. We have done really well from the international break up to this point."
 On Noni Madueke: "He's a great example for the rest of the group because before the first international break he wasn't playing. And what he did is instead of going on holidays he went to Portugal and got somebody to train with him and got in better shape and condition and immediately he got back into the rhythm. You can see now he is full of confidence and trying things and getting past players and he's impacting games with goals and assists and we are very happy with that."
 On the decision not to award Arsenal a penalty: "I don't know, I was confused because when the referee went to the monitor I thought it was because it was a clear penalty. But they made a different decision based off the offside so I don't know, we don't have any clarity yet about the decision."
